initiatives.name: Portfolio Rebalancing: Retail Growth & Office Exit
initiatives.summary: Landsec is executing a strategic pivot to grow its major retail platform by investing up to £1bn while releasing £2bn of capital from offices, reflecting a shift toward higher income-growth, lower-cyclicality assets. This includes scaling back office-led development by at least half.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £1bn retail investment target; £2bn office capital release target

evidence.title: Sale of £705m Low-Returning Assets Portfolio
evidence.summary: Landsec sold £705m of assets including retail parks, London offices, and Queen Anne's Mansions (QAM) as part of its capital recycling strategy to exit low-returning assets. These disposals generated little or no return and were part of a broader plan to release capital from underperforming parts of the portfolio.
evidence.quote: Based on these considerations, we sold £705m of assets over the year. This included £261m of retail parks where the 6.4% income return was reasonable but income growth was limited; a £245m 1970s office block (QAM) which will be vacated in 2028 and requires wholesale redevelopment; £101m of London offices where the 4.9% income return was modest; and £72m of pre-development assets

evidence.title: Exit of Retail and Leisure Parks Portfolio
evidence.summary: Landsec sold four retail/leisure park assets for £261m, exiting 33% of this segment as part of a plan to divest £0.8bn of retail/leisure parks where it has limited scale or competitive advantage. Fewer disposals are expected from this segment going forward as remaining assets have better income profiles.
evidence.quote: We have exited 33% of our retail and leisure parks, which released £261m of capital from assets which generated no real like-for-like income growth, whilst the income yield we sold at was c. 100-150bps lower than income returns for major retail destinations

evidence.title: Portfolio Shift: Retail Investment, Office Capital Release
evidence.summary: Landsec is executing a strategic pivot to grow its major retail platform by investing up to £1bn while releasing £2bn of capital from offices, reflecting a shift toward higher income-growth, lower-cyclicality assets. This includes scaling back office-led development by at least half.
evidence.quote: We aim to invest up to £1bn, funded through recycling further capital out of offices accompanied by disciplined flexibility on book values... We plan to release £2bn of capital employed from offices

initiatives.name: Net Zero Transition Investment Plan (NZTIP)
initiatives.summary: Landsec issued its second Green Bond for £350m in September 2024 to support its transition to net zero, with proceeds fully allocated to four eligible green projects including Timber Square, Thirty High, 5 New Street Square and MYO King's Cross developments.

evidence.title: £135m Net Zero Transition Investment Plan (NZTIP)
evidence.summary: Landsec is investing £135m in its Net Zero Transition Investment Plan to decarbonize its portfolio through air source heat pump retrofits and solar PV installations, supporting its science-based target of 47% emissions reduction by 2030 and net zero by 2040. £88m has been invested to date.
evidence.quote: Our £135m Net Zero Transition Investment Plan (NZTIP) remains central to delivering our SBT, with further investment and implementation during the year. To date, we have invested £88m, including advancing the transition of our office buildings to low-carbon heating and cooling through the air source heat pumps (ASHPs) retrofits and increasing on-site renewable energy generation

evidence.title: Net Zero Transition and Infrastructure Programme (NZTIP)
evidence.summary: Landsec is implementing a Net Zero Transition Infrastructure Programme that includes Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP) retrofits across London offices and solar PV installations at retail assets to improve energy performance and reduce carbon intensity. This contributed to a reduction in building energy intensity despite overall portfolio growth.
evidence.quote: The reduction was primarily driven by improvements across our Workplace portfolio, reflecting the continuous optimisation of existing building systems and the ASHP retrofits across a number of London offices as part of our NZTIP. In addition, energy performance improvements at our retail assets, including the installation of new solar PV system, also contributed to the reduction.

evidence.title: Second Green Bond Issuance of £350m
evidence.summary: Landsec issued its second Green Bond for £350m in September 2024 to support its transition to net zero, with proceeds fully allocated to four eligible green projects including Timber Square, Thirty High, 5 New Street Square and MYO King's Cross developments.
evidence.quote: Following the issuance of our second Green Bond (£350m) in September 2024, supporting our transition to net zero, we published our Green Bond Report 2025, which includes the allocation and impact report.

initiatives.name: Overhead Cost Reduction & Automation Programme
initiatives.summary: Landsec reduced net administrative/overhead expenses by £11m (15%) to £62m, achieving its target of reducing costs to under £65m by FY27 one year early, representing a 26% reduction since FY23. This was driven by new data and tech systems implemented in FY25 enabling automation of core processes.

evidence.title: Overhead Cost Reduction to £62m, 26% Cut Since FY23
evidence.summary: Landsec reduced net administrative/overhead expenses by £11m (15%) to £62m, achieving its target of reducing costs to under £65m by FY27 one year early, representing a 26% reduction since FY23. This was driven by new data and tech systems implemented in FY25 enabling automation of core processes.
evidence.quote: Our overhead costs are down to £62m, marking a reduction of 26% over the last three years. This represents the lowest level in more than 20 years and ensures our income growth flows through to earnings and dividends for shareholders effectively

evidence.title: New Data and Tech Systems Driving Automation
evidence.summary: Landsec implemented new data and technology systems towards the end of FY25 that have driven significant efficiencies across core business processes, including automating the legal lease contract to billing process and enhancing internal reporting capabilities.
evidence.quote: The material reduction in costs principally reflects the benefits of the new data and tech systems we implemented towards the end of FY25. Over the past year, we have started to see significant efficiencies across several core business processes as a result, e.g. by automating the legal lease contract to billing process, and automating and enhancing internal reporting.

evidence.quote: During the year, total energy consumption increased by 4% year on year, primarily due to a 7% increase in absolute floor area following portfolio acquisition, leading to a 3% reduction in energy intensity.

initiatives.name: GHG Emissions Tracking & Reporting Framework
initiatives.summary: Landsec reports and tracks greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, 2, and 3 categories in line with SECR and GHG Protocol requirements, showing year-on-year reductions in Scope 1 and 2 emissions (location-based) from 23,475 tCO2e in FY24 to 21,042 tCO2e in FY26. The company continues to expand its Scope 3 emissions inventory methodology.

The company continues to expand its Scope 3 emissions inventory methodology.
evidence.quote: Total Scope 1 and 2 (location-based method) tCO2e 21,042 23,103 23,475...
